$comment: ★★★ AP6 / plan 06 §5.1 B.13.3 — `artifactProfile: "module"` IS A LIBRARY, SO A MODULE PROJECT BUILDS STANDALONE AND EMITS A REAL ARCHIVE. B.13.3 ruled that `module` is served by every object format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` (the ten `-staticlib`/`-dll`/`-dylib`/`-dyn` formats) and by nothing else. Before that ruling THIS BUILD WAS REJECTED at the AP3 profile-vs-format gate — no format declared `module` in its `artifactProfiles[]`, so every target failed with D_ArtifactProfileNoServingFormat / D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch. The operator's question is the whole reason the ruling exists: *why doesn't a module project emit an artifact? how will it be tested inside its own root project on its own?* A module you cannot build standalone is one you cannot type-check, cannot codegen and cannot get a diagnostic out of — its errors stay invisible until some CONSUMER imports it, and they then surface inside the consumer's build, blaming the wrong project. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED (`module`'s verb is SourceMerge). Orthogonal — which is why this archive is built here and why no example ever links it.
$commentWhyThisExampleExists: ★★ THE CAPABILITY ALREADY HAD A UNIT PIN; WHAT IT DID NOT HAVE WAS A LEG. `tests/program/test_project_config.cpp`, `ModuleIsALibrary.StandaloneModuleBuildEmitsAnArchive`, builds ONE `elf64-x86_64-linux-staticlib` target in-process, asserts rc=0 and the three AP3 diagnostics absent, then reads the first eight bytes back and asserts the `!<arch>\n` ar magic. That is a ONE-HOST, ONE-FORMAT, in-process check: it never touches pe64, aarch64 or Mach-O, and it never leaves the machine that happens to be running it. THIS manifest is the cross-leg half — the in-process corpus runner compiles EVERY declared target on EVERY host (examples/README.md, 'the run gate is runOn, then emulator'), so a green entry here witnesses a module project building standalone for pe64-x86_64, elf64-x86_64, elf64-aarch64 AND macho64-arm64 from Windows, from WSL x86_64 and from macOS. BOTH halves are kept and neither is redundant: delete the unit pin and the archive's BYTES go unchecked; delete this manifest and the capability narrows to one host and one format.
$commentAssertionIsExistenceNotMagic: ⚠ THIS MANIFEST ASSERTS THE ARCHIVE EXISTS AND IS NON-EMPTY — IT DOES NOT ASSERT THE `!<arch>` MAGIC, AND THAT IS A SCOPE DECISION RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. ✔MEASURED: both runners assert artifact PRESENCE and non-emptiness and neither has any vocabulary for asserting CONTENT (`fs::exists` + `fs::file_size`, tests/examples/examples_runner.cpp:1356 and :1377; integrated_tests/runner.cpp:1070-1083). Adding a magic-bytes manifest key to close the gap would introduce a NEW harness mechanism whose only consumer in the entire 596-manifest corpus is this one example — the speculative build §A.2 forbids, and a key with one caller is a key the next reader cannot tell is load-bearing. So the division of labour is deliberate and stated: the MAGIC stays pinned by the unit test named above, which is cheap and already green; the CROSS-LEG, CROSS-FORMAT reach stays here, where the corpus is the only instrument that has it. The claim this file makes is 'four formats, four archives, produced and non-empty, on every leg' — no more.
$commentRunOnIsEmptyDeliberately: ★★ `runOn: []` ON ALL FOUR TARGETS IS THE POINT, NOT AN UNFINISHED FIELD. An `ar` archive is not executable on ANY platform — no host can spawn `textnorm.lib` or `textnorm.a`, and there is no emulator that changes that — so there is no OS this example could honestly name. The empty list is the corpus's existing spelling for a BUILD-ONLY target; before this example the sole precedent was `examples/asm/asm_x86_64_extern_call_object`, whose three arms are all `runOn: []`, making this the SECOND such manifest in the corpus. ✔MEASURED that it routes correctly in the in-process runner: the artifact existence + non-empty + read-back checks all sit BEFORE the `runOn` gate (examples_runner.cpp:1356/:1377/:1393 vs the gate at :1422), deliberately, because 'was an artifact produced' is a question about the COMPILE that a machine unable to spawn the result can still answer. The arm's verdict is `SkippedByRunOn` and the runner logs `produced an artifact but runOn=[] excludes host=…`, so the BUILD is verified and only the SPAWN is declined. ✔Also measured safe under `DSS_STRICT_ARM_VERDICTS=1`: strict mode reds only ENVIRONMENTAL skips, and a `runOn` exclusion is explicitly the manifest's intent (:1850-1854), never an environmental one.
$commentCliRunnerGetsNoVerdict: ⚠⚠ AND IT COSTS THIS EXAMPLE THE CLI RUNNER ENTIRELY, WHICH IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS A REAL HOLE IN THE TWO-RUNNERS RULE RATHER THAN A DETAIL. examples/README.md requires that a capability land in BOTH the in-process harness and the CLI-subprocess one. ✔MEASURED in integrated_tests/runner.cpp:1196-1245: that runner binds the FIRST target whose `runOn` names the host, and when NONE does it prints `[SKIP] … no target's runOn includes host=<host>` and RETURNS WITHOUT COMPILING — its own comment sends the case to 'tests/examples/ in-process runner' by name. So this manifest receives no CLI-subprocess verdict on any host, exactly as its `runOn: []` precedent does not. ★ NO MANIFEST COULD DO BETTER, AND THAT IS THE POINT: after binding a target the CLI runner ALWAYS spawns the artifact (:1141, unconditional — there is no compile-only path between the artifact check and `runBinary`), so naming any host in `runOn` would trade a silent skip for a GUARANTEED red — it would try to execute an archive. Closing the CLI half requires a compile-only verdict IN THE RUNNER (the shape the in-process sibling already has), which is runner work, not manifest work. Weakening this manifest to manufacture a CLI pass would assert something false about what an archive is.
$commentNoOptimizedArm: ⚠ NO `optimizedPipelines`, AND THE OMISSION IS REASONED RATHER THAN FORGOTTEN — examples/README.md's 'Adding a new example' step 3 asks for a `release` arm whenever the feature is runtime-observable, and this one is not. TWO independent reasons, either sufficient. ① NOTHING IS SPAWNED, so an optimized arm would re-emit the same four archives and re-assert the same existence: there is no exit code, no stdout and no runtime behaviour for the arm to preserve, so it could witness only that the optimizer does not crash. The `mustDifferFromBaseline` pin that makes an arm bite cannot be justified either — a differing archive would prove nothing about correctness with no observable to hold fixed — and the honest `$commentByteIdentical` note the alternative needs cannot be written for a target that has no behaviour to compare. ② ✔MEASURED that it would not even COMPILE: `runOneTarget` returns early when the baseline arm's verdict is not `Ran`, ledgering each declared arm with the baseline's reason and `compile not attempted` (examples_runner.cpp:1577-1590, D-TEST-EXAMPLES-CROSS-HOST-RELEASE-ARM-NEVER-COMPILED). Since every arm here is `SkippedByRunOn`, a declared `release` would be a permanently green-looking ledger row that never ran a pass. `asm_x86_64_extern_call_object` omits its arm for exactly reason ②.
$commentArtifactNames: ✔MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — the per-platform extensions below come from `TargetSpec::outputExtension` (src/program/target_spec.cpp:57-59), which for a `container: "archive"` format keys on the closed `ObjectFormatKind` enum: `.lib` for Pe (the Microsoft static-library convention) and `.a` for everything else (Elf and MachO, the Unix convention). Never a format-name branch. The base name is `artifactName.value_or(sourceStem)` (src/program/program.cpp:584), so the project manifest's `"artifactName": "textnorm"` — not the `textnorm.c` stem, which happens to agree — names all four. A project build additionally forces `setPerFormatOutputSubdir(true)`, so each lands at `<outDir>/<formatName>/textnorm<ext>`; `artifact` below is the FILENAME only and both runners compose the subdirectory from `spec` themselves.
$commentRedOnDisable: RED-ON-DISABLE, and the lever is a REAL one rather than a described one: B.13.3 is implemented by the single token `"module"` in the `artifactProfiles[]` array of each serving format descriptor, so deleting that token restores the exact pre-B.13.3 state this example exists to keep from silently returning. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-17 by actually doing it — `"module"` deleted from `elf64-x86_64-linux-staticlib.format.json`'s `artifactProfiles`, nothing recompiled, this project rebuilt through the real CLI: rc=1 and `error[D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch]` (0xD011) — *artifact profile 'module' is not served by object format 'elf64-x86_64-linux-staticlib' (serves: staticlib)* — with an actionable tail enumerating the formats that DO serve it. ★ AND THE WHOLE BUILD DIES, NOT JUST THE MUTATED TARGET: the output tree is EMPTY afterwards, so the other three archives are never written either and all four corpus arms go red at the compile assert, before the artifact check they would otherwise fail at. ⓘ That enumeration is also this file's independent confirmation of the 'ten formats' claim above: with one removed the diagnostic listed exactly NINE survivors (staticlib ×5, `-dyn` ×2, `-dylib` ×2, `-dll` ×1), which is the ten `lib`/`staticlib`-serving formats minus the one deleted. ⚠ Reasoned, NOT measured: the unit pin `ModuleIsALibrary.StandaloneModuleBuildEmitsAnArchive` asserts `countCode(D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch) == 0` on this very format and so must red on the same mutation — stated as a structural consequence rather than an observation, because only the CLI arm above was actually run.
$exitCodeComment: REQUIRED BY THE MANIFEST SCHEMA, ASSERTED BY NOTHING — the same position `asm_x86_64_extern_call_object` documents. Both runners demand an integer `exitCode` on every manifest that is not an `expectDiagnostics` one, and every arm here is `runOn: []`, so the value is never compared against anything. It is 0 because that is the only defensible placeholder for a translation unit with no `main` and no exit; read it as schema tax, not as a pin.
